issue_context.title: kubectl describe job should print key fields for scheduling (suspend, tolerations, nodeSelector)
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

kubectl describe job is missing some key fields. For example, for yaml:
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sample-job
  namespace: default
spec:
  parallelism: 1
  completions: 1
  suspend: true
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      nodeSelector:
        cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-tesla-t4
      containers:
      - name: dummy-job
        image: gcr.io/k8s-staging-perf-tests/sleep:v0.0.3
        args: ["1800s"]
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "100Mi"
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
      restartPolicy: Never
```
`kubectl describe job` returns:

```
Name:             sample-job
Namespace:        default
Selector:         batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
Labels:           batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
                  batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=sample-job
                  controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
                  job-name=sample-job
Annotations:      <none>
Parallelism:      1
Completions:      1
Completion Mode:  NonIndexed
Pods Statuses:    0 Active (0 Ready) / 0 Succeeded / 0 Failed
Pod Template:
  Labels:  batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
           batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=sample-job
           controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
           job-name=sample-job
  Containers:
   dummy-job:
    Image:      gcr.io/k8s-staging-perf-tests/sleep:v0.0.3
    Port:       <none>
    Host Port:  <none>
    Args:
      1800s
    Limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu:  1
    Requests:
      cpu:             100m
      memory:          100Mi
      nvidia.com/gpu:  1
    Environment:       <none>
    Mounts:            <none>
  Volumes:             <none>
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From            Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----            -------
  Normal  Suspended  4s    job-controller  Job suspended
```
**Issue**: some important fields are missing such as `suspend`, `nodeSelector` and `tolerations`.

For comparison, the `kubectl describe pod` contains the relevant information:
```
Name:             sample-job-zkz47
Namespace:        default
Priority:         0
Service Account:  default
Node:             <none>
Labels:           batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
                  batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=sample-job
                  controller-uid=6fb9fe7f-bb73-4e2c-a361-71210724430f
                  job-name=sample-job
Annotations:      <none>
Status:           Pending
IP:               
IPs:              <none>
Controlled By:    Job/sample-job
Containers:
  dummy-job:
    Image:      gcr.io/k8s-staging-perf-tests/sleep:v0.0.3
    Port:       <none>
    Host Port:  <none>
    Args:
      1800s
    Limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu:  1
    Requests:
      cpu:             100m
      memory:          100Mi
      nvidia.com/gpu:  1
    Environment:       <none>
    Mounts:
      /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount from kube-api-access-44x7m (ro)
Conditions:
  Type           Status
  PodScheduled   False 
Volumes:
  kube-api-access-44x7m:
    Type:                    Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources)
    TokenExpirationSeconds:  3607
    ConfigMapName:           kube-root-ca.crt
    ConfigMapOptional:       <nil>
    DownwardAPI:             true
QoS Class:                   Burstable
Node-Selectors:              cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator=nvidia-tesla-t4
Tolerations:                 node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoExecute op=Exists for 300s
                             node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute op=Exists for 300s
                             nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule op=Exists
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From                                   Message
  ...
```

### Why is this needed?

The mentioned fields are important for job scheduling for projects like [Kueue](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue).

The `kubectl describe` command is often used for debugging purposes, but its output might be misleading. For example, seeing the output one may assume the job does not have tolerations or nodeSelector, but it is not possible to tell based on the output.

Hey @mimowo, the tests fail if I don't add the extra spaces here. I think it's due to the alignment of tabs with `Node-Selectors`. See:

```

    --- FAIL: TestDescribeDeployment/deployment_during_the_process_of_rolling_out (0.00s) 
        describe_test.go:2839: expected to find "OldReplicaSets:  bar-001 (2/2 replicas created)" in:                
             Name:               bar                                                                                                          
            Namespace:          foo                                                                                                           
            CreationTimestamp:  Fri, 01 Jan 2021 00:00:00 +0000                                                                               
            Labels:             k8s-app=bar                                                                                                   
            Annotations:        <none>
            Selector:           k8s-app=bar
            Replicas:           2 desired | 1 updated | 3 total | 2 available | 1 unavailable
            StrategyType:                  
            MinReadySeconds:    0     
            Pod Template:                  
              Labels:  k8s-app=bar                                                                                                            
              Containers:       
               :                 
                Image:        mytest-image:v2.0
                Port:         <none>
                Host Port:    <none>
                Environment:  <none>
                Mounts:                        
                  /tmp/vol-bar from vol-bar (rw)
                  /tmp/vol-foo from vol-foo (rw)
              Volumes:              
               vol-foo:
                Type:       EmptyDir (a temporary directory that shares a pod's lifetime)
                Medium:                         
                SizeLimit:  <unset>
               vol-bar:
                Type:          EmptyDir (a temporary directory that shares a pod's lifetime)
                Medium:        
                SizeLimit:     <unset>
              Node-Selectors:  <none>
              Tolerations:     <none>                                                                                                         
            OldReplicaSets:    bar-001 (2/2 replicas created)
            NewReplicaSet:     bar-002 (1/1 replicas created)
            Events:                  
              Type    Reason             Age                From                   Message
              ----    ------             ----               ----                   -------
              Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  12m (x3 over 20m)  deployment-controller  Scaled up replica set bar-002 to 1
              Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  10m                deployment-controller  Scaled up replica set bar-001 to 2
              Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  2m                 deployment-controller  Scaled up replica set bar-002 to 1
              Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  60s                deployment-controller  Scaled down replica set bar-002 to 1
```

I see, indeed the values for `Node-Selectors` `Tolerations` and `OldReplicaSets` are aligned in the full output. 

Out of curiosity, I'm wondering where is the code / mechanism which determines the shift of `OldReplicaSets` to align it. Can you find it out?  So that we better understand the intent, because some values are out of alignment, for example `Volumes.vol-foo.Type`.

This is the code for the empty dir volume: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d2b16b2/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L1028-L1039
From reading the code, the value should be aligned, as it seems just a tab. This is the code for `OldReplicaSets`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d2b16b2/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L4372-L4375
Could we test that these fields are actually printed? The `Deployment` describer ends up using this function so its test case in `describer_test.go` would be a good candidate to extend
